thread:
Alex: FYI proposing we reduce SIEM raw-export retention in S3 from 400d -> 90d to cut PII surface and storage spend. Need a JIT snapshot + approval runbook for IR/legal to get 1y when required. Also KMS unwrap flow guidance. Thoughts?
Maria: Quick clarifying Q — is this regulatory-driven or a cost/privacy push? That changes exception handling.
Alex: Mixed. Privacy wants minimization by default; infra flagged cost. Legal/IR want ability to preserve 1y+ for investigations. My idea: tiered buckets + preserve hooks.
Jon: Our SOC partner expects 400d access for historical queries. How do we avoid breaking their pipelines?
Sam: For partners keep an anonymized/aggregated export for 365d and raw for 90d. Implementation sketch:
- nightly job: write raw -> raw-events (90d), scrubbed -> partner-exports (365d)
- partner-exports uses partner CMK + cross-account role
- raw-events encrypted with our CMK; forensic-snapshots copy for 365d with HSM-wrapped CMK
Also SSO-proxy can mint timeboxed creds for analysts to fetch snapshots.
security-automation: created ticket SEC-5120: "SIEM export retention + JIT snapshot flow" https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-5120
Maria: Legal hold requirement: need automated preserve hook to pin specific case objects beyond default TTL. Must be immutable and auditable.
Alex: Implementation idea:
- tag export objects with x-redwood-case=CASE-YYYY-NNN
- retention controller (OPA) enforces TTL unless case tag present
- unwraps require documented approval + short TTL KMS grant
Sample S3 tag + OPA pseudo-rule:
````
Tag: x-redwood-case: CASE-2026-987
OPA rule (pseudo): allow_preserve { input.object.tags["x-redwood-case"] != "" }
````
Jon: Critical: how do we audit unwraps and snapshot downloads? IR needs a clear trail.
Sam: KMS + CloudTrail + explicit audit entries. Pattern:
- Envelope encrypt objects with CMK
- Use KMS grants for decryption; track grants in CloudTrail
- Every unwrap request must map to ticket id and an approver; create ephemeral service principal per-request
- Emit a security-log entry for each unwrap: case_id, grant_id, requester, approver, time, reason
Example audit entry (stringified JSON we index):
````
{"ts":"2026-03-15T18:22:31Z","event":"snapshot_unwrap","case_id":"CASE-2026-987","grant_id":"g-0a1b2c3d","requester":"jon","approver":"maria","object":"s3://forensics/CASE-2026-987-20260315.tar.gz"}
````
Maria: We must engage Privacy on scrub rules and Finance for cost projection before locking retention numbers.
Alex: Proposed next steps:
1) PR: architecture + playbook + ticket template + OPA snippets + sample audit schema
2) SEC-5120 stakeholder board: security, IR, legal, privacy, infra
3) 2-week canary moving non-critical indices to 90d to validate search & SLAs
4) build JIT unwrap flow + audit event emission
Jon: Tests: simulate expired-object deny in staging (OPA deny), ensure preserved-case retrieval works with approval grant. I want an automated test matrix.
Sam: Will add automated test plan: create object w/ ttl=10s, wait 12s -> expect OPA deny + 403; then add x-redwood-case tag and perform approval -> expect allowed download with audit record.
